title: fix(rest): /export writes a date or datetime cell with a four-digit year, so an export of a year below 1000 re-imports (#20602)
body:
Fixes #20602
Clause-②: no

## What changes

`GET /api/v1/data/:object/export` wrote a `date` or `datetime` cell's year unpadded, so a year from 0001 to 0999 left the export short (`500-01-01`, `500-01-01 10:00:00`) and `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import`, which reads a four-digit year only since PR #20601, refused the platform's own file.

One source file changes, `packages/rest/src/export-format.ts`, on the three paths triage named:

- `formatDate`'s `date` branch (base `:327`), `utcWallClock` (base `:234`) and `zonedWallClock` (base `:275`) now take the day from one private helper, `calendarDay`.
- **The pad rule: core's `temporalStorageForm`, `date` rule, imported from `@objectstack/core`** (not mirrored). It is the storage form the write doors keep and the rule `/import`'s reader (`parseDateCell`) spells an instant's day with. It pads 0001..0999 and leaves a year outside 0001..9999 unpadded. `@objectstack/rest` already depends on `@objectstack/core`; no `packages/core/**` edit.
- `zonedWallClock` no longer reads the year from `Intl`'s `year` part. That part is an ERA year: year 0 (1 BC) reads `1`, so padding it would spell `0001-01-01T03:00:00Z` in New York (still 31 December of year 0 there) as `0001-12-31`, a date a year later that `/import` would take. The zone's year is the instant's UTC year, plus one when the zone has reached January while UTC is in December, minus one the other way round (an offset is under a day). The day is built with `setUTCFullYear`, never `Date.UTC`, which reads 0..99 as 1900..1999.
- `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` is untouched (read-only for this card); the pins drive the real routes.

## Measured

Harness for every route reading below: the real `POST /api/v1/data/:object`, `GET /api/v1/data/:object/export` and `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import` handlers of a `RestServer` over `ObjectQL` plus `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3 `:memory:`) and the real metadata protocol, driven in-process; the business timezone is what the resolved `ExecutionContext` carries.

**H0, confirmed** at the base `6981abfd26`, host `TZ=America/New_York`. A row created through the create door (201) with `date` `0500-01-01` and `datetime` `0500-01-01T10:00:00.000Z` exports, in CSV, xlsx (text cells) and JSON alike:

| business timezone | `date` cell | `datetime` cell | re-import through `/import` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| none | `500-01-01` | `500-01-01 10:00:00` | row refused, `invalid_date` (`Day: "500-01-01" is not a valid date`) |
| Asia/Shanghai | `500-01-01` | `500-01-01 18:05:43` | refused, `invalid_date` |
| America/New_York | `500-01-01` | `500-01-01 05:03:58` | refused, `invalid_date` |

A row carrying only the `datetime` is refused on that cell too (`At: "500-01-01 10:00:00" is not a valid datetime`). The 2026 control exported and re-imported unchanged. The odd seconds are the tz database's local mean time for a year before either zone kept standard time; the import reads them back through the same database, so the round trip holds (pinned).

At the head, the same probe exports `0500-01-01` and `0500-01-01 10:00:00` / `18:05:43` / `05:03:58`, and every row re-imports as `0500-01-01` and `0500-01-01T10:00:00.000Z` in all nine format and zone pairs.

**H1, confirmed**, a one-shot census of `formatCellValue`, base file against head file: years 0001, 0050, 0500, 0999, 1000, 2026, 9999 plus 0000, -000001 and +010000; days 01-01, 07-15 and 12-31; `date` plus `datetime` at 00:00, 03:00, 10:00 and 23:30 UTC; zones none, `UTC`, Asia/Shanghai, America/New_York, Pacific/Kiritimati, Pacific/Pago_Pago and an unknown zone. 1050 cells:

- Source years 1000, 2026, 9999 and +010000: every cell byte-identical except 5 whose zone day is `0999-12-31` (a 1000-01-01 instant in New York or Kiritimati), now padded.
- Source years 0001..0999: every cell padded, except 2 whose zone day is already `1000-01-01` (identical) and 5 whose zone day is in year 0 (base spelled the era year, `1-12-31`; head spells the rule's `0-12-31`).
- Out of range, 0000 and -000001 (refused by the write doors): every `date` and every UTC / no-zone `datetime` cell identical; a zoned `datetime` now spells the year the rule does (`0-…`, `-1-…`) instead of the era year (`1-…`, `2-…`), 94 cells, and 2 cells whose zone day is `0001-01-01` are padded. `/import` refuses every one of these spellings, before and after.

**H2, confirmed for the pinned years.** Created, exported and re-imported into a fresh stack, stored values identical: `date` for 0001, 0050, 0500, 0999, 1000, 2026, 9999 and `datetime` for 0500, 0999, 1000, 2026, 9999, in CSV, xlsx and JSON, with no business timezone, Asia/Shanghai and America/New_York. **Not identity for a `datetime` in years 0001..0099**: see the first acceptance note.

**H3, confirmed.** Two ablations, each through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode (anchor hit once, the blob moved `8904e5c4b1b4` to a new hash, restore proven: blob equals HEAD `8904e5c4b1b4` and `git diff HEAD` empty). The subject is `src/` (relative imports; no `dist` in the path), so no rebuild leg.

- `calendarDay` returns the unpadded spelling: `82 failed | 61 passed (143)`, the same 82 tests the unfixed base fails; none of the 82 names 1000, 2026 or 9999.
- The zone year taken from `Intl`'s era year again: `1 failed | 142 passed (143)`, exactly the year-boundary pin.

## Tests

New file `packages/rest/src/export-date-year-pad.test.ts`, 143 tests: the formatter census (every year, `date` and `datetime`, zones none / UTC / Asia/Shanghai / America/New_York / unknown), the 2026 control's exact cells, `Date` and epoch-ms inputs, the year-boundary pin, and the route round trip per year, format and business timezone. The xlsx leg also asserts the exported cells are text, not dates.

All at `e739a50fa0` (the branch after merging `origin/main` `05cb2bc030`):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest run test`: `Test Files 228 passed (228)`, `Tests 4527 passed | 52 skipped (4579)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest run test:repo`: `Tests 8 passed (8)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest run typecheck`: exit 0, `check:test-typecheck: OK`; `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new test file.
- The public surface of `@objectstack/rest` is byte-unchanged (`calendarDay` is private; no export moved), so no downstream consumer owes a test.

## Gates

At `e739a50fa0`:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`: 60 commands, all exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` first exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, no `dist`), and are green after `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'`. `--ran`: `60 derived, 60 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- Artifact rosters: 33 rows run (the five `@objectstack/spec` rows skipped: no `packages/spec` path; the 18 checker-health `--self-test` rows not run), 30 exit 0; `check-closing-target-claim`, `check-partof-closing-keyword` and `check-single-claim-paths` need this PR's context and are read after it opens.
- `pnpm lint` (the whole tree, not narrowed): exit 0, 37s.
- `node scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0, 4 citations, all resolve.

## Acceptance notes

1. **Landing order: a `datetime` in years 0001..0099 now round-trips silently wrong until #20599's core fix lands.** Measured at the routes on the head: a `datetime` `0050-01-01T10:00:00.000Z` exports as `0050-01-01 10:00:00` and `/import` stores `1950-01-01T10:00:00.000Z` (`0001` stores `1901-…`; under Asia/Shanghai `1950-01-01T10:05:43.000Z`), `ok 3, errors 0`, in CSV, xlsx and JSON. At the base the cell was `50-01-01 10:00:00`, which `/import` refused. The export's spelling is now the correct one; the misread is `Date.UTC`'s two-digit-year remap in core's `zonedWallClockToUtcMs`, the first site of #20599, which remains open and is out of this card's file surface (`packages/core/**` is read-only here). A hand-written cell `0050-01-01 10:00` is already stored in 1950 today (#20599's own `reach:`); this change adds the platform's own export as a second producer of that cell. Recommendation in the report: land after that fix. The year 0100 control round-trips exactly.
2. **Out-of-range years in a business timezone.** A `datetime` whose zone day falls in year 0 or before now spells the rule's year (`0-12-31`) instead of the era year (`1-12-31`). Both spellings are refused by `/import`, and the write doors refuse such years; no in-range cell moves except by padding.
3. **Not changed, dormant:** `packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts` `xlsxDateToNaiveCell` spells an xlsx date cell's year unpadded. An xlsx date cell is an Excel serial, which starts in 1900 (1904 on the Mac date system), and the export writes text cells, never date cells, so no workbook reaches it with a year below 1000. Noted, not filed.

## Declared narrowing, verbatim

**Declared narrowing — verification ran UNLOCKED.** `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`
could not take the shared verify lock on this host: no usable `flock`. The shared
verify lock is declared Linux-only (`flock` is util-linux, and a stock macOS does
not ship it), so the command below was run directly, without the lock —
a declared narrowing, not a silent one. No serialization guarantee held for this
run, nor for any sibling agent in this container while it ran.

    pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/rest^...' build
    pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2 src/export-date-year-pad.test.ts
    node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs … -- pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2 src/export-date-year-pad.test.ts   (two ablations)
    pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/rest...' build
    pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest run test
    pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest run test:repo
    pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest run typecheck
    pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*' --concurrency=2

The same paragraph was printed for each command above and for the throwaway probe runs behind H0 and the note-1 reading (temporary test files, deleted; not in the diff).
